title: Rehearsal under its own throwaway root (decision 9): the 4 stopped mechanisms fire
description: Decision 9 (ruling 2026-10-21) lets the rehearsal mint its own root inside its temporary directory, so the fedatario act, the delegation ceiling, fork plus contest and disposal by distinguish can fire without the operator's keys.
acceptance_criteria: examples/rehearsal/run_rehearsal.py gains a mode (flag or default; justify the choice in the handoff) that generates a fresh root key with ssh-keygen inside the temporary directory the script itself created, enrols it as the SANDBOX trust root (the sandbox copy of trust/ only), and mints the same 9 W-002 names with fresh keys through warrant.py's own draft and apply verbs, signing the draft with the sandbox root the way the operator signs (ssh-keygen -Y sign). The sandbox constitutional reputation file is re-signed with the sandbox root so phase B still verifies in the sandbox.

Under that root the story attempts, through the tools' CLIs only: a fedatario act signed and verified; a delegation with a ceiling used within it and refused beyond it; a fork under one name detected by attest.py forks and contested by a different name, the contested act carrying no weight (PR-022 clause 4); a case disposed by the distinguish verb, visible in precedent.py disposition-ratio's by_citation column. The shipped sign verb appends at the tip by design, so the fork may be produced only by writing one sibling act file outside the verb; the scorecard labels that step a simulated forger, and detection must be the tool's.
Every row that depends on the sandbox root says so in its label or evidence: signed under the rehearsal root, not the operator's.

The live tree is never written: the existing integrity check still passes. A new test copies a rehearsal warrant into a scratch copy of the repository (never the working tree) and asserts warrant.py refuses it there, because its root is not the enrolled one.

Never read ~/.ssh/harness_root, and never read private material under the live .harness/keys, .harness/trust or .harness/constitutional. No private key leaves the temporary directory, which is still removed by default (T-442).
The 8 rows that fired before still fire. westphalia_kpi.py stays blocked with the tool's own message (a second registry needs a ratified record, PR-029 clause 6). Contracts stay unbuilt.
A test in .harness/tests asserts the evidence of each newly fired row. The suite passes via goal_mode. Do not edit CLAUDE.md. Hand off to verifier.

Add a live-tree-isolation test (copy a rehearsal warrant into a scratch repo copy, assert warrant.py refuses it) and evidence tests for each newly-fired row.

REJECTED (verifier harness-verifier, T-445 criteria): replayed the happy path exactly as claimed -- python3 examples/rehearsal/run_rehearsal.py --json gave fired=12 blocked=1 unbuilt=1 of 14, live_tree_untouched=true; python3 -m pytest .harness/tests/test_rehearsal.py -q gave 14 passed; python3 .harness/bin/goal_mode.py run --cmd "python3 -m pytest .harness/tests -q" gave GOAL REACHED on iteration 1/3 (134s). grep of run_rehearsal.py/test_rehearsal.py for home()/expanduser/ssh-harness_root path construction found none (all hits are prose/docstring, matching the claim no code path reads ~/.ssh/harness_root or live .harness/keys,trust,constitutional). RehearsalRootIsNotTheLiveRootTests passed in the full suite.

BUT T-445's own mandated mutant #2 ("stop distinguish from recording a disposal -- the matching row must stop reporting fired") is NOT caught. Reproduced in a throwaway copy outside the working tree (never the live .harness/bin/precedent.py): commented out the `dispose_case(hroot, args.case, "distinguish", ...)` call inside cmd_distinguish (precedent.py ~line 1253), leaving attest.sign_act + the by_citation counter untouched. Result: `python3 examples/rehearsal/run_rehearsal.py --json` still reports the "a case disposed by `distinguish`" row as fired (evidence still shows by_citation_raw=1), and `python3 -m pytest .harness/tests/test_rehearsal.py -q` still reports 14 passed -- including DecisionNineMechanismsFireTests.test_the_by_citation_disposal_now_fires. Direct inspection of the sandbox's own case file (--keep run) confirms the case itself (C-006 in that run) stays status="open", disposal=None even though the scorecard calls it "a case disposed by distinguish". By contrast, the other two T-445-mandated mutants ARE caught correctly: neutering attest.py's forks() to return [] flips the fork row to blocked and fails 2 tests (test_the_fork_is_detected_and_contested, test_total_outcome_counts); disabling the DELEGATION CEILING raise in attest.py's sign_act flips the delegation row to blocked and fails the matching 2 tests. Only the distinguish-disposal mutant escapes.

Root cause: disposition_counts()'s by_citation_raw counts signed `distinguish` acts (attest chain), not case-record disposal status, so the scorecard's fired/blocked check (`disp_ratio3_json.get("by_citation_raw",0)>=1`) and the new test's assertion (`by_citation_raw=1` in evidence string) are both insensitive to whether `dispose_case()` actually ran. The acceptance criterion's own wording is "a case disposed by the distinguish verb" -- the test as written does not verify the CASE was disposed, only that an act existed and a counter moved. This is a genuine gap in T-444's own acceptance-criterion-7 test coverage ("A test in .harness/tests asserts the evidence of each newly fired row"), not a pre-existing/unrelated precedent.py defect out of scope -- test_rehearsal.py is one of T-444's two changed files.

Ask: strengthen DecisionNineMechanismsFireTests.test_the_by_citation_disposal_now_fires (or the scorecard row's own condition in run_rehearsal.py) to also assert the case's own disposal, e.g. via `precedent.py case show <case3_id>` reporting Status: disposed / Disposal: distinguish, so a regression that breaks dispose_case() while leaving the act-signing/counter path intact is actually caught. Everything else in the hand-off (sandbox isolation, the other 3 newly-fired rows, the 8 previously-fired rows, westphalia/contracts staying blocked/unbuilt, goal_mode full-suite pass) replayed clean and is not in question.
